hypotheses.belief: 80% S&P ranges should be 1.6x the VIX-implied move (rule 5, lesson L3).
hypotheses.plain: Over years of data a 1.6x range held 98% of the time since 2022, far more than 80%. It is right for a shock month like November 2026 but far too wide in normal times. Proposal: size ranges from recent realized volatility (the adaptive band) instead of a fixed 1.6x.

hypotheses.belief: 80% VIX bands should be +/-25% of the prior close for one day (rule 5).
hypotheses.plain: A +/-25% one-day VIX band held 99% of days since 2022. Too wide in normal markets; the adaptive band keeps close to 80% and still widens in a storm.

hypotheses.belief: Size 80% S&P ranges from half VIX + half recent realized vol, width fitted before 2022.
hypotheses.plain: Fitted on 2016-2021, it held 77% from 2022 on, close to the 80% target. But it held only 53% in the last 15 days, so in a shock it still runs narrow. Proposal: use the wider of the adaptive band and the VIX-implied band once VIX is above 25.

hypotheses.belief: Don't default to 'up' after a falling week (lesson L4).
hypotheses.plain: After a week down 2%+, the next day was up 52% of the time since 2022 (normal 53%). Historically falling weeks did NOT make up days rarer, so L4 as a rule of thumb is not supported by the long record; it may still be right in a specific regime.

hypotheses.belief: When 3-month VIX is below VIX (inverted curve), the next week moves closer to what VIX prices.
hypotheses.plain: When the VIX curve inverts, the following week realizes much more of the VIX-implied move than usual, in both halves of history. Proposal: when inverted, do not shrink ranges below the VIX-implied move.

hypotheses.belief: The setup playbook's 'P(up in 5 days)' from look-alike days beats the plain up-rate.
hypotheses.plain: Tested since 2022 on 245 days using only earlier history: analogs scored 0.245 vs 0.244 for the plain up-rate (lower is better). They do not beat the base rate, so treat the playbook as a picture of the range of outcomes, not as a forecast.

hypotheses.belief: At least one specialist analyst beats the plain up-rate on next-day calls.
hypotheses.plain: Best analyst (rates) scored 0.2481 vs 0.2484 for the plain up-rate across ~1,950 out-of-sample days. A gap that small is noise: none of the simple signals predicts tomorrow's direction.

rule: The loop only proposes. method/notes changes need Rk's approval.
